title: The empty van
caption: I bought a Chevy Express and sold off the shelving and dividers that came in the back. An empty box — and the start of everything.

title: Cleaning it out
caption: A big vacuum at the car wash to get the cargo bay back to bare metal, then a wash at sunset out of a single Home Depot bucket. Clean slate.

title: Sound deadening
caption: Kilmat on the panels — the quiet layer you never see once the walls go up, but you hear it on every drive.

title: The floor
caption: Templated the floor with Amazon boxes and paper bags, cut XPS foam and then a full sheet of plywood with a jigsaw, test-fit until the edges were right, then tidied the van back up. The moment the floor went down, the box suddenly felt like a room.

title: A hole in the roof
caption: First time cutting into a roof — a little nervous. A frame from leftover wood, pilot holes, a jigsaw, butyl tape to seal, and the fan going in. Not just ventilation: the line where a work truck starts becoming a home.

title: Wall insulation
caption: Threaded nylon rope through the ribs — which felt a lot like motion planning — then packed Havelock wool over the ceiling and walls, held with the rope and 3M spray. Every redo was just the search for a better way.

title: On the road
caption: Out to Joshua Tree mid-build — the reason for all of it. Open desert, a warm glow through the windows at dusk, a chair set up inside. Still a build in progress, already a life on the road.

title: The walls
caption: Cutting and fitting the plywood walls — the last big skin over the wool, and where the raw metal box finally disappears.

title: The bed frame
caption: Sketched the frame by hand first — front, side, the whole thing in perspective — then cut the lumber and taped the pieces up against the wall to check the height before driving a single screw. Raised just enough to slide the bins, the cooler, and the camp chairs underneath. The first real piece of furniture, and the moment the van finally had a floor plan.
